Best-Worst Scaling method used with human evaluators comparing pairs of system outputs

Evaluators were presented with two summaries and the input document and asked to decide which one was better based on accuracy (does the summary contain accurate facts?), informativeness (is important information captured?), and fluency (is the summary written in well-formed French?).
Best-Worst Scaling: annotators compare pairs of system outputs and choose the better and worse summary according to specified criteria.

We asked evaluators to base their judgments on accuracy (does the summary contain accurate facts?), informativeness (is important information captured?) and fluency (is the summary written in well-formed French?).

overall_notes: The paper focuses on NLG evaluation for French text summarization using both automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) and human evaluation with Best-Worst Scaling. The extraction was generally accurate but contained some redundant information that was consolidated.
